I will keep it simple and plant the crop pattern I know best here in Quzhou: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. Around here that is the steadiest way for me to earn grain and cash from one year, and at 78 I care more about a reliable, familiar system than about chasing a risky high-return crop. I will not take on cotton, vegetables, or anything that needs too much hand labor, too much market watching, or too many field visits. I can manage wheat and maize with machinery services, a few key irrigations, and straightforward fertilizer use.

For wheat, I will stay with an improved variety rather than a hybrid because seed cost is lower and the management is something I already understand. I will use moderate fertilizer, not excessive fertilizer, because water is always something I must think about on the North China Plain, and I do not want to spend more just to create lodging, disease, or wasted input. I will irrigate at the critical times and spray only when needed for the usual diseases and insects. For maize after wheat harvest, I will use a hybrid because the yield advantage is worth it. I will sow quickly after wheat, keep the fertilizer balanced, irrigate a couple of times if moisture is short, and manage weeds and insects with a small number of timely applications. I will rely on rotary tillage because it is practical, easy to arrange, and fits how I would manage land at my age.
